question.value: How long do giant molecular clouds live, how long do clouds and young H-alpha regions coexist before dispersal, and how do these time-scales vary with galactic environment, measured from the cloud-scale de-correlation of CO and H-alpha emission in nine nearby disc galaxies

evidence.quote: Progress has been hampered by a lack of robust empirical constraints on the giant molecular cloud (GMC) lifecycle.
find a universal de-correlation between molecular gas and young stars on GMC scales, allowing us to quantify the underlying evolutionary timeline

claims.hypothesis: Do molecular gas and young stars de-correlate on GMC scales across a range of nearby disc galaxies, implying rapid evolutionary cycling?
claims.experiment: Tuning-fork analysis of CO-to-H-alpha flux ratio bias versus aperture size in nine PHANGS galaxies
claims.result: All nine galaxies show de-correlation that strengthens at smaller aperture sizes
claims.finding: De-correlation is a universal feature, implying rapid cycling between gas, star formation and feedback

evidence.quote: All galaxies in our sample exhibit a pronounced de-correlation between gas emission and SFR emission, which becomes stronger as the aperture size decreases.

claims.hypothesis: Are GMCs long-lived or transient, and does the lifetime vary with environment?
claims.experiment: Fit the HEISENBERG model to each galaxy and to radial bins
claims.result: t_CO is 9.6-30.5 Myr across galaxies, with factor of about 2 variation within galaxies
claims.finding: Clouds are short-lived transient objects whose lifetime depends on environment

evidence.quote: We find that the derived molecular cloud lifetimes are relatively short and vary with galactic environment: they range between 10 and 30 Myr across our galaxy sample.

claims.hypothesis: What drives cloud dispersal and when does massive star formation appear in the cloud lifecycle?
claims.experiment: Measure the CO and H-alpha overlap time t_fb relative to the cloud lifetime
claims.result: Unembedded massive star formation appears after 75-90 per cent of the cloud lifetime; t_fb is 1-5 Myr
claims.finding: Early stellar feedback (photoionisation, winds) disperses the cloud rapidly after massive stars emerge

evidence.quote: it seems inescapable to conclude that unembedded high-mass star formation arrives late during the cloud lifecycle, after $75{-}90$ per cent of the cloud lifetime
this implies that, in these environments, early feedback mechanisms such as winds, photoionisation or radiation pressure must be the dominant processes driving the destruction of molecular clouds

claims.experiment: Compute the integrated efficiency per event from t_CO, Sigma_SFR and the filtered Sigma_gas
claims.finding: Star formation is fast and inefficient in all nine galaxies

evidence.quote: The combination of a short $t_{\rm CO}$ and low $\epsilon_{\rm sf}$ indicates that star formation is fast and inefficient, for all galaxies in our sample.

claims.hypothesis: Is the cloud lifetime set by galactic dynamics or by internal cloud dynamics, depending on gas surface density?
claims.experiment: Compare t_CO in radial bins with tau_gal, t_ff and t_cr, splitting at a kpc-scale molecular gas surface density
claims.result: Above about 8 Msun/pc^2 t_CO tracks tau_gal; below it t_CO tracks t_cr and t_ff
claims.finding: Two regimes: galactic dynamics at high density, internal dynamics at low density

evidence.quote: the transition between cloud lifetimes being governed by galactic dynamics versus cloud lifetimes being set by cloud internal dynamics seems to occur at a molecular gas surface density averaged across the galactocentric radial rings
Future work with a larger sample of galaxies will need to refine this division.

claims.hypothesis: Do morphological features such as co-rotation and bars affect the measured cloud lifetime?
claims.experiment: Inspect radial-bin t_CO relative to co-rotation radii and bar regions
claims.result: Longer lifetimes at some co-rotation bins; extreme values in some bar-end bins
claims.finding: Co-rotation can elevate lifetimes and bar-end bursts bias t_CO

evidence.quote: Some influence of co-rotation on the molecular cloud lifetime is suggested in several galaxies in Figure

why_this_data.value: CO(2-1) chosen because it is brighter and easier to map across whole galaxies at arcsecond resolution than dense-gas tracers

evidence.quote: it is brighter and easier to observe than these high density gas tracers, allowing entire galaxies to be mapped efficiently at arcsecond resolution

why_this_method.value: The statistical method avoids subjective cloud classification and needs only the region separation length, not individual GMCs, to be resolved

evidence.quote: Rather than needing to resolve individual GMCs, as was the case in previous methods, this new technique only requires resolving the mean separation length of the combined population of GMCs and Hii regions

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using a CPROPS cloud catalogue for GMC radii and masses was rejected in favour of HEISENBERG outputs

evidence.quote: By contrast, using a cloud catalogue would rely on subjective classification.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: The very bright NGC628 'headlight' cloud was masked; leaving it in raises t_CO and makes one bin unconstrained

evidence.quote: and becomes unconstrained in the bin including the ‘headlight’ cloud, with a lower limit of 25.1 Myr

how_they_decided_enough.value: Each radial bin needs at least 50 peaks per tracer for adequate statistics

evidence.loc: 5.1 Radial profiles of the molecular cloud lifetime
evidence.quote: we require that each bin contains a minimum of 50 peaks identified in our full-galaxy runs for each tracer, to ensure sufficient statistics to constrain the derived quantities to sufficiently high precision

limitations_admitted.value: No spatially resolved internal extinction correction, so embedded star formation may be missed

evidence.quote: our lack of a spatially-resolved extinction correction may cause us to underestimate emission from young, embedded Hii regions, or fail to detect them at all

limitations_admitted.value: Feedback times and separation lengths for NGC4254, NGC4303, NGC4321 and NGC4535 may be upper limits because of coarser resolution

evidence.quote: We therefore advise some caution in the interpretation of the feedback time-scales measured for NGC4254, NGC4303, NGC4321, and NGC4535.

limitations_admitted.value: Spatially resolved star formation histories are unknown, so the constant-SFH requirement cannot be tested

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, the spatially-resolved SFHs of the galaxies in our sample are not known.

limitations_admitted.value: Bursty bins at bar tips violate the method assumptions and bias t_CO

evidence.quote: Both of these extremes bias the measured cloud lifetimes.

limitations_admitted.value: The analytical model is simple and does not separate gas phases

evidence.quote: The analytical predictions from (cite: Jeffreson2018) are based on a simple analytical model, which limits the direct comparison with our measurement.

referee_caveats_inferred: Peak-identification and aperture parameters were hand-optimised per galaxy; no systematic sensitivity table is given
A uniform 30 per cent [NII] correction and a single global extinction rescaling may bias H-alpha peak fluxes
The 8 Msun/pc^2 regime boundary rests on a few dozen radial bins with no formal significance test
Heavy reliance on unpublished in-prep inputs (PHANGS maps, H-alpha maps, inclinations, CPROPS catalogues)
Absolute time-scales depend on one calibrated reference time-scale from a separate simulation paper

products_in_archive.value: PHANGS v1.0 data release integrated-intensity maps used; public availability not stated in this paper

evidence.quote: We use the "broad" integrated intensity maps of the PHANGS v1.0 data release (A. K. Leroy et al. in prep.).

code_released.value: HEISENBERG described in Kruijssen et al. 2018; public release or availability not stated here

evidence.quote: Our analysis method is formalised in the HEISENBERG code, which is presented and described in detail by (cite: Kruijssen2018).
